question.text: In a Master-Feeder Structure for a cross-border AIF, where is the management fee TYPICALLY charged?

answer.text: Only at master fund level; feeder usually charges a symbolic fixed fee (e.g., USD 1,000)
Only at feeder fund level; master fund is fee-free
Equally split between master and each feeder fund
At the investor level directly, bypassing both master and feeder

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 8.5.3: in master-feeder, management fees are charged at the master fund level; feeder funds charge only a symbolic absolute amount (like USD 1,000). The main fee expense passes through via NAV allocation from master to feeder. The Trap: Option A inverts the flow. Option C complicates unnecessarily. Option D fabricates an investor-direct fee model. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B/C test fee flows in cross-border structures. XIX-C is exam-specific on feeder mechanics. Manager's Pro-Tip: When you have multiple feeders (Mauritius + Singapore), verify that the master NAV allocation does not accidentally result in higher effective fees for one feeder — LPs in higher-fee feeder will rapidly demand MFN.
